rationale: almabench is a small, compute-bound floating-point benchmark (AM1 pseudo-potential integration) dominated by a few hot numeric loops and heavy double-precision arithmetic, so the highest value comes from cheap, value-preserving arithmetic obfuscation: SUB gets the strongest weights since algebraic/substitute transformations thrive on dense integer and FP arithmetic with modest overhead; SPLIT is favored for its near-zero runtime cost and good diversity contribution across the benchmark's loop bodies. BCF and FLA are kept at mid weights — they meaningfully impede static analysis of the control flow but the hot inner loops make their runtime cost a real concern, so moderate RuntimeCost weights let the feature-driven selector apply them selectively to cold functions. IBR and ICALL are down-weighted because branch/opaque-predicate insertion and indirect-call conversion add per-iteration overhead precisely where this program spends all its time, and ICALL carries extra CorrectnessRisk with few indirect-call sites to hide. IGV is included at moderate weight — the benchmark's numeric constant tables benefit from global-value hiding — but with an elevated CorrectnessRisk weight since tampering with FP constants can silently alter numerical results. Overall the table biases the selector toward arithmetic and structural diversity while gating control-flow-heavy passes by their runtime cost.
